text:
maya: ran nvprof on the 16-GPU sparse-attn replay job this morning. timeline CSV attached, but quick summary: huge idle gaps right after KV-merge kernels and before all-reduce starts.

owen: can you paste the nvprof cmd you used? was this with kernel selection toggles on?

maya: `nvprof --profile-from-start off --events gld_32b_loads,dram_read_transactions --log-file nvprof_sparse.csv --csv ./bin/replay --args ...`  (I turned off autostart to skip warmup noise)

maya: also instrumented our custom timers: `timer:kvcache_lookup`, `timer:kvmerge_wait`, `timer:allreduce_start`, `timer:allreduce_end`, `timer:kernel_select`. CSV shows kvmerge_wait spikes up to 120ms on non-leader shards.

alex: interesting — that suggests comm/compute overlap failing: processes hit a barrier waiting on KV merge completion before they post their allreduce. could be scheduling noise or an unexpected memcpy.

samir: did you see any PCIe or NVLink stall events in nvprof? those often correlate.

maya: there are `dram_read_transactions` bursts but no obvious PCIe stall metric. however `gld_32b_loads` drops during the same gaps. Looks like compute threads spin while waiting on a small memcpy + kernel selection decision.

owen: our kernel selection path queries architecture tables and does some branching on sequence length distribution — might be a pre-kernel CPU-side decision that serializes launches.

alex: could be this: we do a single-threaded kernel selector that checks quantization-friendly kernels and then calls `cudaMemcpyAsync` for meta buffers. On some ranks that ends up being the critical path.

maya: i dumped wall-clock timestamps from our timers:
``` 
1919004327 timer:kernel_select start
1919004329 timer:kernel_select end   (2ms)
1919004329 timer:kvmerge_wait start
1919004350 timer:kvmerge_wait end   (21ms)
1919004350 timer:allreduce_start
1919004351 timer:allreduce_end    (0.5ms)
```
Gives the image of compute -> long kvmerge gap -> tiny allreduce.

samir: 21ms kvmerge wait is substantial. Are we blocking on per-token prefetch/deserialize? Could microbatch ordering cause head-of-line blocking?

maya: yes, microbatch sizes vary. Batching heuristic currently groups by request arrival, not by sequence length. So a long sequence can trigger extra kv work and stall peers.

owen: two quick experiments: 1) force kernel_selection to the fastest generic path (skip quantization checks) to see if gaps vanish; 2) fuse KV-merge memcpy & posting to NCCL into a single CUDA stream so we don't serialize CPU->GPU ops.

infra-bot: perf-run queued: 1919005000; will run variants: kernel-select=fast, kvcache-prefetch=batched, stream-fuse=true.

alex: also add an nvprof stack trace capture around the kernel_select function to confirm CPU-side blocking location (`nvprof --profile-child-processes --callgraph all`).

maya: good call. i'll also add a tiny custom counter emitted just before allreduce_post to capture the lapse from last kernel to nccl post (helps when nvprof sampling misses short events).

samir: longer term: adjust batching heuristic to limit heterogeneous sequence grouping and try small sequence-first scheduling. That should reduce head-of-line kv spikes.

owen: +1. Also consider making kernel selection parallel (per-device worker) and move non-critical checks off the hot path.

maya: next steps: run infra-bot variants, collect nvprof CSV + our timers, and if kvmerge_wait reduces to <3ms we can mark a perf regression fix. If not, we'll dig into NVLink counters.

alex: thanks. please drop the nvprof CSV and the timers log here when ready. :thumbsup:

maya: will post when the queued runs finish (ETA ~10m).

infra-bot: perf-run 1919005000 completed. results uploaded to: https://redwood-internal/storage/perf/1919005000/nvprof_sparse.zip :white_check_mark:

maya: downloading now, starting quick diff against baseline and will report back with top-3 hypotheses.

owen: ack, thanks everyone.
